question: How can a series of successive cognitions produce the manifestation of a single object?
premises: Inferential cognition may involve a series of successive cognitions, such as smoke and so on.
Each member of that series may arise clearly.
Inference requires the manifestation of one unified object or conclusion.
inference: A merely successive series of clear cognitions cannot by itself account for the manifestation of one unified object.
plain_english: Moreover, even if a clear series of successive cognitions of smoke and so on arises, how could that produce the manifestation of a single thing?
